title: Define the MVP and record client-side platform access
body:
Goal: the agreed MVP scope and the architecture change are written down before the M2 roadmap.
Acceptance: `docs/milestone2-mvp.md` holds decisions D1-D24, the MAL API findings and the Google sign-in and Play findings; `docs/future-features.md` lists the parked ideas with the decision each came from; ADR 0007 (client-side platform access) is accepted and listed in `docs/decisions/README.md` and the root README; CLAUDE.md and the README replace the rule that only the server talks to MAL (module list, architecture diagram, Auth section); `docs/tickets-m2.csv` holds the M2 prep tickets; relative links resolve.
Out of scope: skill changes (M2-0c), agent changes (M2-0a, M2-0b), the M2 roadmap.
Skill: adr, ticket-workflow.

title: Rewrite the existing agents with project knowledge
body:
Goal: the six agents in `.claude/agents/` know this project, so the main session gets useful, compact output instead of generic answers.
Acceptance: every agent has a `description` saying when to use it, `tools`, `model`, `skills:` (only skills it needs on every call), a body with the project facts it cannot guess, a fixed report format, and the hard rules (no commits or pushes, `git add` new files, never spawn agents, stay in the given scope). Per agent:
- `Explore` (haiku; Read, Grep, Glob; skill codebase-overview): module map, package convention `com.greenzean.animekmp.<module>.<feature>`, where the SDL, SQLDelight `.sq` files, Flyway migrations, Koin modules and ADRs live. Answer: a direct answer, then at most ~15 `path:line` hits, no file dumps, a plain not found when nothing matches.
- `build-runner` (haiku; Bash, Read): command table matching CI (lint `./gradlew spotlessCheck detekt`; Android `./gradlew :androidApp:assembleDebug :shared:allTests`; server `./gradlew :server:build`, which needs Docker for Testcontainers, say so if it is down; schema `./gradlew :server:test -PupdateSchema`). Plain `./gradlew` commands without pipes so the gradle-filter hook trims output. On failure, read `build/reports/tests/` or the detekt reports for the cause. Report PASS/FAIL per task, then per failure the task, test, `file:line`, a 1-3 line error and the likely cause. Never edit files or run `spotlessApply` unless asked.
- `docs` (haiku; Read, Write, Edit; skills adr, ticket-workflow): doc types and their formats: ADRs (template, numbering, index and README links, status), ticket text (Goal, Depends on, Acceptance, Out of scope, Skill; CSV columns as in `docs/tickets-m0-m1.csv`), README sections, `docs/milestone2-mvp.md` and `docs/future-features.md` (D-numbers). Short sentences, tables for comparisons. Never invent decisions, versions or URLs; list gaps under Missing.
- `researcher` (sonnet; Read, WebSearch, WebFetch): stack context (KMP/CMP, AGP 9, Ktor, graphql-kotlin, Apollo Kotlin, SQLDelight, Koin, Exposed, Flyway, Postgres, MAL API v2, Google Credential Manager). Source priority: official docs and release notes, then Maven Central or Google Maven, then GitHub releases; blogs never as the primary source. Versions: newest stable at least two weeks old, with its release date. Output per question: answer, URL, checked date, confidence (read directly, from a summary, unverified), ready to paste into an ADR Context.
- `reviewer` (opus, high; Read, Grep, Glob, Bash; skills ticket-workflow, codebase-overview): steps `gh issue view <n>`, `git diff main...HEAD` plus uncommitted changes, check every acceptance criterion and out-of-scope item; check the CLAUDE.md code rules, ADR 0007, scope to the named modules, tests in `commonTest` and the server, SDL committed and in sync, ADR written when a decision changed. Output: verdict, criteria checklist (met, not met, not verifiable), findings by severity with `path:line`. Bash only for read-only git and gh.
- `security-reviewer` (opus, high; Read, Grep, Glob; skill sync-protocol): threat model for this repo: public repo and untrusted client; ADR 0007 (MAL tokens only on the device in Keystore-backed storage, no platform tokens or platform user data on the server); Google ID token checks (signature, `aud` = web client ID, `iss`, `exp`, nonce, users keyed on `sub`); our session tokens; per-user authorization in every resolver (user ID from the token, never from input); GraphQL depth, complexity and batch-size limits; `pushChanges` input validation; secrets, `.env` and keystores; CI on fork PRs; MAL agreement limits (no stored credentials, privacy policy); Play account deletion. Output: findings with severity, `path:line`, exploit scenario and fix.
Verified: every frontmatter parses, tool names exist and each `skills:` entry matches a folder in `.claude/skills/`; smoke runs of `Explore` (where is the pull cursor stored?), `build-runner` (lint only) and `docs` (format a one-line test ticket without writing a file) follow their report formats.
Out of scope: new agents (M2-0b), changes to skills, settings or hooks.
Skill: ticket-workflow.

title: Create the area agents
body:
Goal: the area agents planned in CLAUDE.md exist, so large M2 features can be split by module.
Depends on: M2-0a (reuses its hard rules and report format).
Acceptance: five agents, all sonnet with tools Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash. Common body: implement only the given part of a ticket inside the agent's module(s) and report anything outside instead of changing it; follow the preloaded skills and the ADRs; run the module's tests and `./gradlew spotlessCheck detekt` itself with plain `./gradlew` (subagents cannot call build-runner); `git add` new files; no commits or pushes; never spawn agents. Report: files changed, tests run and their result, deviations from the plan, open questions. Per agent:
- `server` (skills ktor-server-conventions, postgres-migrations, graphql-schema, sync-protocol): `server/` only. Schema changes go server first; the SDL is regenerated with `./gradlew :server:test -PupdateSchema`, never edited by hand. Never calls MAL (ADR 0007). Tests: `:server:test`.
- `shared-kmp` (skills kmp-data-layer, kmp-error-handling, kmp-di-koin, sync-protocol, graphql-schema): `shared/` (`commonMain` and platform `actual`s), plus `androidApp/` only for platform wiring such as WorkManager. The MAL client lives here, with tokens behind a secure-storage interface. Tests: `:shared:allTests`.
- `compose-ui` (skills kmp-compose-ui, kmp-presentation-mvi, kmp-navigation): `composeApp/` only. Uses the view model interface it is given and reports needed view model changes instead of making them. Previews and accessibility. Build: `:androidApp:assembleDebug`.
- `tester` (skills kmp-testing, postgres-migrations): writes and fixes tests only (`commonTest`, `server/src/test`); fakes over mocks, Testcontainers for the database. Does not change production code; reports bugs it finds.
- `build-ci` (skill kmp-module-structure): `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, the `build.gradle.kts` files, `.github/workflows/`, `config/detekt`, `.editorconfig`, `docker-compose.yml`, `Dockerfile`. Every version change comes with a source and release date; no secrets in workflows; fork PRs get no secrets.
- `CLAUDE.md` Delegation updated: the area agents exist; keep only for large features and the feature order; add that area agents run their own Gradle checks.
Verified: every frontmatter parses, tool names exist and each `skills:` entry matches a folder in `.claude/skills/`; after a session restart `/agents` lists all 11 project agents.
Out of scope: changes to the existing six agents (M2-0a), skills, settings or hooks.
Skill: ticket-workflow, kmp-module-structure.

title: Align skills with ADR 0007
body:
Goal: the skills stop saying that the server talks to MAL, matching ADR 0007.
Depends on: M2-0 (ADR 0007).
Acceptance: `codebase-overview`: `shared/` lists the MAL client and says only the app talks to MAL; `server/` says it syncs libraries between a user's devices, never calls MAL and stores no platform tokens, platform user data or anime metadata; `docs/` mentions `milestone2-mvp.md`. `kmp-module-structure`: the module tree shows the MAL client in `shared/` and no MAL adapter in `server/`. `ktor-server-conventions`: the intro rule matches ADR 0007, and the not-decided-yet note names auth (Google ID token verification, session tokens) instead of the MAL adapter. `grep -rn 'MAL adapter\|talks to MAL' .claude/` finds no old-rule text.
Out of scope: agents (M2-0a, M2-0b), other skills.
Skill: codebase-overview, kmp-module-structure, ktor-server-conventions.

title: Write the M2 roadmap
body:
Goal: the MVP decisions D1-D24 are split into ordered tickets with dependencies.
Acceptance: `docs/m2-roadmap.md` lists the tickets in order with dependencies and the D-numbers each covers; every D-number maps to at least one ticket; the tickets are rows in `docs/tickets-m2.csv`; relative links resolve.
Out of scope: creating the GitHub issues, any code.
Skill: ticket-workflow.

title: Spike: MAL API with a real client ID
body:
Goal: replace the unconfirmed MAL API points with tested facts. Time-box 1 to 2 days.
Depends on: a MAL client ID registered by the user.
Acceptance: tested with a real client ID: search and details with only `X-MAL-CLIENT-ID`; the `recommendations` field on details (shape, size); `/anime/suggestions` response shape and the empty list for new users; rate-limit behaviour and the 403 block; which app type MAL offers when registering and whether PKCE `plain` works without a secret; list read and write (`/users/@me/animelist`); decision in `docs/decisions/0008-mal-api.md` (caching, backoff, fields to request); `docs/milestone2-mvp.md` findings updated.
Out of scope: production MAL client code.
Covers: D5, D10, D11, D13, D14. Skill: adr.

title: Server stores IDs only: drop the dev catalog
body:
Goal: the server holds library entries and anime IDs, not anime details (ADR 0007).
Depends on: M2-2.
Acceptance: decision on entries referencing `mal_id` directly or the `anime` table becoming an ID map, written in an ADR; Flyway migration drops `title` and any other anime detail from the server; the debug dev catalog is removed; the SDL is regenerated and committed; the client sync path follows the new shape; sync tests and the Testcontainers migration test pass; existing local libraries still sync.
Out of scope: accounts (M2-4).
Covers: D2, D19. Skills: sync-protocol, postgres-migrations, graphql-schema, adr.

title: Server: Google sign-in and session tokens
body:
Goal: the server accepts a Google ID token and issues its own session token.
Depends on: M2-3.
Acceptance: `signInWithGoogle` mutation; ID token checked for signature (Google's rotating keys), `aud` = web client ID, `iss`, `exp` and nonce; users table keyed on `sub`, no email used as the key; session token (short-lived access plus refresh) signed with a secret from env; token and client ID config in `.env.example`; tests with a fake key set for each check that must fail; SDL committed.
Out of scope: the Android sign-in UI (M2-6), authorizing sync (M2-5).
Covers: D24. Skills: graphql-schema, ktor-server-conventions, postgres-migrations.

title: Server: authorize sync per user
body:
Goal: every sync operation runs as the signed-in user; the hardcoded dev user is gone.
Depends on: M2-4.
Acceptance: `pushChanges` and `changesSince` read the user ID from the session token, never from input; entries of one user are never visible to another (tests with two users); unauthenticated calls are rejected with a typed error; the client sends the session token and refreshes it on expiry; dev user removed from server and client.
Out of scope: the sign-in UI (M2-6).
Covers: D2, D24. Skills: sync-protocol, graphql-schema.

title: App: Google sign-in and optional account
body:
Goal: the user can sign in with Google; the app still works fully without an account.
Depends on: M2-4.
Acceptance: Credential Manager with the Sign in with Google library behind an interface (`expect/actual` or Android-only implementation in `androidApp`); versions rechecked on Maven; ID token sent to `signInWithGoogle`; session token in Keystore-backed secure storage; account state in a view model (signed out / signed in); sign-in screen reachable from settings, never required to use the app; view model tests with fakes.
Out of scope: merging the local library (M2-7), account deletion (M2-8).
Covers: D1, D24. Skills: kmp-presentation-mvi, kmp-data-layer, kmp-di-koin.

title: First login merge and logout choice
body:
Goal: signing in does not lose data and signing out lets the user decide.
Depends on: M2-5, M2-6.
Acceptance: on first login on a device with a library, its entries are merged into the account automatically (pending changes pushed, account entries pulled, last-write-wins as in ADR 0006); on logout the app asks whether to keep or delete the library on the device; tests for both paths including a library with entries on two devices.
Out of scope: MAL linking (M2-21).
Covers: D18, D20. Skill: sync-protocol.

title: Account deletion in the app and on the web
body:
Goal: meet the Play account-deletion policy.
Depends on: M2-5, M2-6.
Acceptance: `deleteAccount` mutation removes the user, entries and tombstones in one transaction; in-app delete flow with confirmation; a public web page (served by the server) explains and starts deletion; declared in the Data safety form notes; data kept for security or legal reasons is listed; server test proves nothing remains for the user.
Out of scope: the Play listing (M2-26).
Covers: D22. Skills: graphql-schema, postgres-migrations.

title: App: MAL login with PKCE
body:
Goal: the user can log in to MAL on this device and the app keeps the tokens safely.
Depends on: M2-2.
Acceptance: authorization code with PKCE (`plain`), no client secret; browser redirect handled behind an interface; access and refresh tokens in Keystore-backed storage, never sent to our server; refresh on expiry; logout deletes the tokens; MAL client ID read from config (public); typed errors; tests with a fake MAL server (Ktor MockEngine).
Out of scope: using the tokens for list sync (M2-17, M2-19).
Covers: D1, D3, D4. Skills: kmp-data-layer, kmp-error-handling, kmp-di-koin.

title: App: MAL search and details with cache and backoff
body:
Goal: search for anime and load details through MAL, cached on the device.
Depends on: M2-2.
Acceptance: Ktor MAL client with the `X-MAL-CLIENT-ID` header; search and details calls with the fields chosen in ADR 0008; results cached in SQLDelight with an expiry (client-side caching only as long as reasonably necessary); backoff and stop on HTTP 403; offline returns a typed `NoConnection` error; tests with MockEngine and an in-memory database.
Out of scope: screens (M2-11).
Covers: D5, D10. Skills: kmp-data-layer, kmp-error-handling.

title: Search for new anime screen
body:
Goal: the user searches MAL and adds an anime to their library.
Depends on: M2-10, M2-14.
Acceptance: search screen with debounce, results with image, title and add action; offline shows that searching for new anime needs a connection; adding writes to the local database only; previews and accessibility labels; view model tests.
Out of scope: library search (M2-13).
Covers: D10. Skills: kmp-presentation-mvi, kmp-compose-ui, kmp-navigation.

title: Personal suggestions screen
body:
Goal: show MAL's personal suggestions for the logged-in user.
Depends on: M2-9, M2-10.
Acceptance: `GET /anime/suggestions` call and screen; without a MAL login, or with an empty list, the screen explains why and shows nothing; items can be added to the library; view model tests for logged out, empty, error and success.
Out of scope: per-anime recommendations (future features).
Covers: D11. Skills: kmp-presentation-mvi, kmp-compose-ui.

title: Library search, filter and sort on the device
body:
Goal: find entries in the user's own library, offline.
Acceptance: SQLDelight queries for title search, status filter and sort by title, score or last updated; UI on the library screen; tombstoned entries never shown; tests with an in-memory database.
Out of scope: filters by genre, year or type (future features).
Covers: D9. Skills: kmp-data-layer, kmp-presentation-mvi.

title: Library entry: five statuses and score 1-10
body:
Goal: the entry model matches MAL: status, episode progress and score.
Acceptance: statuses Watching, Completed, On hold, Dropped, Plan to watch (map to MAL's values) in the local database, sync and server; score 1-10 (or unset) validated on the client and in `pushChanges`; edit UI for status, progress and score; migrations for existing data; SDL committed; tests.
Out of scope: dates, rewatch count, notes (future features).
Covers: D6, D7, D12. Skills: sync-protocol, graphql-schema, postgres-migrations.

title: Import a MAL export file
body:
Goal: the user imports an exported MAL list from a file, no login needed.
Depends on: M2-14.
Acceptance: file picker behind an interface; parser for MAL's XML export (including gzip) with tests on a sample file; entries merged into the local library; entries that already exist and differ are reported, handled by the conflict feature once M2-20 lands (until then the local entry is kept); summary of added, skipped and invalid entries.
Out of scope: API import (M2-17).
Covers: D16. Skills: kmp-data-layer, kmp-testing.

title: Export the library as a MAL file
body:
Goal: the user saves their library in MAL's export format.
Depends on: M2-14.
Acceptance: writer for MAL's XML format; save through a platform file API behind an interface; round trip test (export, import, same entries); only this format.
Out of scope: CSV or JSON export (future features).
Covers: D16, D23. Skill: kmp-data-layer.

title: Import the library from MAL by login
body:
Goal: a logged-in user pulls their MAL list into the app.
Depends on: M2-9, M2-14, M2-18.
Acceptance: paged read of `/users/@me/animelist` respecting backoff; mapped to local entries; entries that differ go to the conflict flow from M2-18; progress shown; resumable after a failure; tests with MockEngine.
Out of scope: automatic ongoing sync (M2-19, M2-20).
Covers: D16. Skills: kmp-data-layer, kmp-error-handling.

title: Design: user decides on conflicts
body:
Goal: a written design for D15 before sync code depends on it. Time-box 1 day.
Depends on: M2-2.
Acceptance: ADR 0009 states what counts as a conflict (same anime, different status, progress or score; timestamps available from MAL), what the user can choose (keep app, keep MAL, per entry or for all), where unresolved conflicts are stored, how this interacts with last-write-wins on our server and with MAL linked on one device only; UI sketch; test cases listed.
Out of scope: implementation (M2-20).
Covers: D15. Skills: adr, sync-protocol.

title: Send app changes to MAL automatically
body:
Goal: every change made on this device reaches MAL when the user is logged in to MAL.
Depends on: M2-9, M2-14.
Acceptance: outbox of changes to push to MAL in SQLDelight; sender runs as background work behind an interface (WorkManager on Android) with connectivity constraint and retry with backoff; only changes made on this device are sent, not changes pulled from our server (D17); idempotent; failures keep the change queued; tests with fakes for the scheduler and MAL client.
Out of scope: pulling MAL changes (M2-20).
Covers: D13, D17. Skills: kmp-data-layer, sync-protocol.

title: Two-way MAL sync with conflict choice
body:
Goal: changes made on MAL's website come into the app; conflicts are decided by the user.
Depends on: M2-18, M2-19.
Acceptance: periodic background pull of the MAL list; differences applied automatically when there is no conflict; conflicts shown and resolved as designed in ADR 0009; resolved choice is synced to MAL and our server; tests for no conflict, conflict kept local, conflict kept MAL, and offline.
Out of scope: devices without MAL (M2-21).
Covers: D14, D15. Skills: sync-protocol, kmp-presentation-mvi.

title: MAL on several devices
body:
Goal: the account knows MAL is linked, and a device without MAL asks the user what to do.
Depends on: M2-5, M2-9, M2-20.
Acceptance: server stores only the platform name ("MAL") as linked for the user, no username or ID (D19); device with synced entries but no MAL login offers: log in to MAL, or keep the library local to our account; changes pulled from our server are never pushed to MAL by that device (D17); server and client tests; SDL committed.
Out of scope: other platforms.
Covers: D15, D17, D19. Skills: sync-protocol, graphql-schema, postgres-migrations.

title: Server hardening: query limits and input validation
body:
Goal: the public GraphQL endpoint resists abuse.
Depends on: M2-5.
Acceptance: query depth and complexity limits, batch-size limit on `pushChanges`, request size limit, rate limiting per user and IP; input validation for every field (lengths, ranges, enums); introspection decision documented; tests for each limit.
Out of scope: hosting (M2-23, M2-24).
Covers: D22. Skills: graphql-schema, ktor-server-conventions.

title: Spike: where to host the server
body:
Goal: pick the host for the Ktor server and Postgres. Time-box 1 day.
Acceptance: ADR 0010 compares at least three options on price, free tier limits, Postgres backups, HTTPS, region and effort (verified with the researcher agent, with dates); decision and monthly cost estimate.
Out of scope: deploying.
Covers: D22. Skill: adr.

title: Deploy the server
body:
Goal: the server runs online with HTTPS and a managed database.
Depends on: M2-22, M2-23.
Acceptance: production Dockerfile; environment config documented (no secrets in the repo); Flyway migrations run on start; JSON logs; health check; database backups verified by a restore; the app has a release server URL; deploy steps in the README.
Out of scope: CD automation unless trivial.
Covers: D22. Skills: ktor-server-conventions, postgres-migrations.

title: Privacy policy and MAL agreement compliance
body:
Goal: the legal pages Play and MAL require exist.
Depends on: M2-8.
Acceptance: privacy policy (data stored on the server: Google `sub`, library entries and anime IDs, linked platform name; data on the device; MAL data and caching; deletion) served from a public URL; MAL consent shown before MAL login; checklist against the MAL agreement (no credentials stored, cache only as needed, removal within 24 hours on request, no scraping, no revenue); contact for removal requests.
Out of scope: legal review.
Covers: D22. Skill: adr.

title: Release build and Google Play listing
body:
Goal: the app is on a Play test track.
Depends on: M2-24, M2-25.
Acceptance: release build type with R8 and a keystore kept out of the repo; signed AAB built in CI from secrets; applicationId and version set; store listing, screenshots, Data safety form and account-deletion URL; content rating; internal testing track published; target API level meets Play's current requirement (verified).
Out of scope: production rollout.
Covers: D21, D22. Skill: kmp-module-structure.

title: M2 checkpoint: end-to-end
body:
Goal: prove the MVP.
Depends on: all other M2 tickets.
Acceptance: on a clean install with no account: add anime, search, filter, rate, export and import a file; sign in with Google on two devices and see the same library; log in to MAL, import, change on both sides and resolve a conflict; delete the account; result note in `docs/m2-result.md`; CI, lint and tests pass on main.
Out of scope: new features; fixes go in follow-up bug tickets unless trivial.
Checkpoint: every D1-D24 verified or listed as not met.

title: Server: sign-out revokes the refresh token
body:
Goal: signing out also ends the session on the server, so a refresh token copied off the device stops working at once instead of after its 30 days.
Depends on: M2-4, M2-7.
Acceptance: a `signOut` mutation (authenticated by the refresh token) revokes the whole token family and returns a result that does not reveal whether the token existed; repeating it, or sending an unknown or already revoked token, is not an error; the SDL file and the schema drift test are updated and the Apollo operation is added; the app calls it during sign-out (after the keep-or-delete choice) and signs out locally even when the call fails or the device is offline; server tests cover revoke, repeat and a refresh with the revoked token (`UNAUTHENTICATED`); app tests cover the offline sign-out; ADR 0011 consequences and ADR 0010 are updated through a new ADR or a superseding note, not by rewriting an accepted one.
Out of scope: "sign out everywhere" (revoking every device's family), cleaning up expired token rows, rate limiting, changing the keep-or-delete behaviour.
Covers: follow-up to D20 (ADR 0011). Skill: graphql-schema, ktor-server-conventions.
Order: server schema first, then the app.

title: Mini PC runs everything except the apps; server and DB deploy after passing tests
body:
Goal: the Mac runs only the Android app, the emulator and Gradle builds; the server, PostgreSQL and Docker run on the mini PC. Server and DB changes are deployed to the mini PC automatically whenever the automated server tests pass, without asking.
Acceptance: `docker` and `docker compose` cannot run on the Mac from Claude Code sessions (the `docker compose *` and `docker info *` allow entries are removed from `.claude/settings.local.json` and a deny rule or hook blocks them); `scripts/dev-server.sh` no longer starts Postgres through local compose and targets the mini PC; a `server-deploy` script outside the repo (like `server-tests`) syncs the server build over SSH, applies the Flyway migrations, restarts the server and checks health; CLAUDE.md "Where things run" says that after `server-tests` passes, `server-deploy` runs without asking, and that no deploy runs when the tests fail or were not run; the Definition of Done in the `ticket-workflow` skill gets a "deployed and healthy" item for tickets that touch `server/`; a failed deploy is reported with its output and not retried silently; a new ADR (next free number) records the rule and is linked from `docs/decisions/README.md`; no host, address, user or key is in the repo.
Out of scope: production Dockerfile and hosting choice (M2-23, M2-24), a CI deploy job, exposing the server to the internet.
Covers: working rules in CLAUDE.md. Skill: ktor-server-conventions, postgres-migrations.
Order: settings and script first, then docs.
